name: spatial_transport_trap
description: og-03 thermophoretic trap behind the swappable spatial_transport face. The live, default solver is a genuine 1-D FiPy finite-volume accumulation column (model_spatial_transport='fipy', runs anywhere, backs every canonical run). The face also lets you swap in a dolfinx FEM solver with a Soret-drift weak-form term (model_spatial_transport='fenics') — that class only registers today and is not yet active (dolfinx is conda-only and its solver extension is on a held branch, so it raises a 'run under pixi' error in the canonical venv). assert_face is enforced at build. Same pore physics, one live solver plus a swappable FEM alternative (plan 4.5).

flow_velocity.description: Buoyant convective flow in the pore (m/s); 0 = no-convection control

pore.doc:
Real 1-D FiPy finite-volume accumulation column for the Baaske thermal
trap. Reads the pore temperature, the convective flow velocity and the
porosity; derives the thermophoretic + convective accumulation velocity;
solves the steady column with the genuine FiPy FVM solver; and emits the
enrichment factor (read from the solved profile), the residence time and the
FVM balance residual (overwrite sensors — the current state of the trap).

_contract.summary: Real 1-D FiPy accumulation column for the Baaske thermal trap: thermophoresis + convection concentrate a dilute feed, enrichment exponential in pore length.
_contract.description: Derives the accumulation velocity from the pore's thermophoretic (Soret) and convective physics (Pe_conv = flow*width/D; beta = geom*soret*dT*Pe_conv/width * confinement; w_acc = D*beta) and solves the steady 1-D column 0 = D c'' - w_acc c' with the genuine FiPy finite-volume solver (feed at the top, no-flux trapped base). The enrichment factor is READ from the solved base/top ratio (not assigned), reproducing Baaske's exponential length-scaling: >10^8-fold in favorable geometry, ~1 in a no-gradient/no-flow control. All outputs are overwrite sensors; the FVM residual is the spatial-flux-conservation witness.

inputs.flow_velocity: buoyant convective flow speed in the pore (meter/second)
inputs.porosity: pore porosity / openness (dimensionless, 0-1; lower = more confinement = more trapping)

math: beta = geom * soret_coeff * delta_T * Pe_conv / pore_width * (1 - porosity_openness)
0 = D c'' - D*beta c'  ->  enrichment = c_base / c_top = exp(beta * pore_length)
assumptions: Accumulation-column reduced model of the thermal trap (Debye 1939; Baaske 2007): enrichment exponential in pore length.
w_acc from thermophoretic (Soret) drift coupled to buoyant convection; geom calibrates the trap efficiency to the Baaske magnitude.
Steady FVM solve each step (fast relative to pore evolution).

emitter.doc:
Store historical states in memory.

``subsample`` records only every Nth composite tick (default 1 =
every tick). Use this for long runs or composites with heavy
state (large fields, many agents) to keep RAM bounded — the
saved time-series still reflects the simulation's true cadence
via each row's ``global_time`` field.

``max_len`` optionally bounds ``history`` to the most recent N
recorded rows (a ring buffer): once the cap is reached each new
record drops the oldest. Default ``None`` = unbounded (the
historical behaviour — consumers such as v2ecoli that read the
full ``history`` are unaffected unless they opt in). ``max_len``
counts *recorded* rows (i.e. post-``subsample``).
